fact: Mead treats a dog as running at large whenever it is off its owner's or keeper's premises and not held by a leash, cord or chain no longer than 6 feet.
quote: A dog shall be deemed to be running at large when off or away from the premises of the owner, possessor, keeper or his or her agent or servant or a member of his or her immediate family, and not restrained, either by leash, cord or chain of not more than six (6) feet in length.
source_label: Mead Municipal Code Sec. 7-6-310 (codified through Ord. No. 1075, April 14, 2025)
notes: Read through the Municode API (job "Supplement 20", codified through Ord. No. 1075); the library page renders by script. Ordinances adopted after April 14, 2025 would not show, so re-check against the Town once its site is reachable.

fact: Mead allows no more than four dogs and cats in any combination over six months old on one premises, except at a zoned and licensed kennel, pet shop or veterinary clinic.
quote: There shall be kept no more than four (4) dogs or four (4) cats, or any combination thereof equaling four (4) animals, more than six (6) months of age on any one (1) premises at any one (1) time. Young animals under six (6) months of age or until weaned may be kept without being counted toward the allowable number of animals. This Section shall not apply to: (1) A zoned and licensed veterinary clinic or hospital operated by a licensed veterinarian which retains animals for veterinary medical care. (2) A zoned and licensed pet shop. (3) A zoned and licensed kennel or animal boarding facility.
source_label: Mead Municipal Code Sec. 7-6-300 (codified through Ord. No. 1075, April 14, 2025)
notes: Read through the Municode API (job "Supplement 20", codified through Ord. No. 1075); the library page renders by script. Ordinances adopted after April 14, 2025 would not show, so re-check against the Town once its site is reachable. Land Use Code Sec. 16-3-60(d)(1) repeats the four-animal limit but counts animals over four months of age.

fact: Since HB21-1222, Colorado law has every local government treat a family child care home as a residential use in its zoning, land use, fire, sanitation and building rules.
quote: ACCORDINGLY, LOCAL GOVERNING AUTHORITIES SHALL TREAT FAMILY CHILD CARE HOMES AS RESIDENTIAL PROPERTY USE IN THE APPLICATION OF LOCAL REGULATIONS, INCLUDING ZONING, LAND USE DEVELOPMENT, FIRE AND LIFE SAFETY, SANITATION, AND BUILDING CODES. LOCAL GOVERNING AUTHORITIES SHALL NOT IMPOSE ANY ADDITIONAL REGULATIONS GOVERNING FAMILY CHILD CARE HOMES THAT DO NOT ALSO APPLY TO OTHER RESIDENTIAL PROPERTIES
source_label: HB21-1222 signed act, C.R.S. 26-6-104.5(1)(b) as amended (signed June 7, 2021)
notes: Statewide rule kept in Mead's file because the Mead playground page uses it to mark the town's by-right home-daycare zoning as state-driven (own: false). Signing date from the bill page leg.colorado.gov/bills/hb21-1222. The child care statutes have since moved to Title 26.5; the page cites the bill, not a current section number.

fact: Colorado's family child care home rules require at least 6 inches of resilient surfacing in the use zone of climbing or sliding equipment 18 inches or higher, list artificial turf with a built-in resilient pad as an approved solid surface, and want the maker's written statement that new solid surfacing meets current federal requirements.
quote: a. All climbing equipment, sliding equipment, or equipment with attached platforms, eighteen (18) inches or higher must have resilient surfacing of at least six (6) inches in the use zone, see rule section 2.337(B)(3), surrounding the equipment. b. Department-approved resilient surfacing includes loose fill materials such as wood chips, wood mulch, engineered wood fiber, pea gravel, synthetic pea gravel, shredded rubber tires, and sand. Solid unitary materials include poured in place surfacing, approved rubber mats, playground tiles, and artificial turf with built in resilient pad. … 1) Any newly installed solid unitary materials used for resilient materials must have written documentation from the manufacturer stating the material meets current federal requirements. 2. Maximum height of equipment a. The maximum height of toddler climbing equipment, sliding equipment, or equipment with attached platforms cannot exceed thirty-two (32) inches. … 3. Use zone a. Toddler climbing equipment, sliding equipment, or equipment with attached platforms must have a three (3) foot use zone surrounding the equipment. Toddler slides require a six (6) foot use zone extending out from the base of the slide. b. Preschool and school-age climbing equipment, sliding equipment, or equipment with attached platforms must have a six (6) foot use zone surrounding the equipment.
source_label: Colorado Department of Early Childhood, 8 CCR 1402-1-2.337(B), family child care home outdoor equipment and surfaces (47 CR 04, effective March 16, 2024), via Cornell LII
notes: Statewide rule, own: false on the page. Cornell LII shows the version effective 3/16/2024; re-check against the CDEC rule set on the Secretary of State site.

fact: Mead's code settles who owns and maintains public open space case by case at review, generally with the Town keeping neighborhood, community and pocket parks and public trails and an HOA or the landowner keeping landscaped outlots and private recreation facilities.
quote: Ownership and maintenance of public open space shall be determined by the Town on a case by case basis through the review process. a. Generally, the Town shall own and maintain neighborhood parks, community parks, pocket parks and public trails. b. Landscaped outlots and private recreational facilities shall be owned and maintained by a homeowners' association or the landowner.
source_label: Mead Municipal Code Sec. 16-2-120 (codified through Ord. No. 1075, April 14, 2025)
notes: Read through the Municode API (job "Supplement 20", codified through Ord. No. 1075) on 2026-09-25; the library page renders by script. Ordinances adopted after April 14, 2025 would not show, so re-check against the Town once its site is reachable.

fact: Mead requires a Town license for every dog and cat six months or older, and each license runs from January 1 to December 31 of the year it is bought.
quote: No person shall own, harbor, have custody of or keep any domestic dog or domestic cat of six (6) months of age or older in the Town without first obtaining a license therefor from the Town. … Each dog or cat license obtained shall be valid between January 1 and December 31 of the year purchased unless sooner revoked.
source_label: Mead Municipal Code Secs. 7-6-210 and 7-6-230 (codified through Ord. No. 1075, April 14, 2025)
notes: Read through the Municode API (job "Supplement 20", codified through Ord. No. 1075) on 2026-09-25; the library page renders by script. Ordinances adopted after April 14, 2025 would not show, so re-check against the Town once its site is reachable. Sec. 7-6-220 leaves the fee to a Board of Trustees resolution; no fee is stated on pages.

fact: Mead lets household pets be kept on a lot of any size, within the four-pet limit and the article's housing and control rules.
quote: Household pets may be kept regardless of the size of the premises, provided that the number is limited as provided in Section 7-6-300 and they are housed, penned and controlled in the manner prescribed by this Article.
source_label: Mead Municipal Code Sec. 7-6-70 (codified through Ord. No. 1075, April 14, 2025)
